okay, i've just been out for about 2 hours driving this model around country lanes, lots of turns and cars in the road, motorways and roundabouts

gonna break my review down into sections and compare this mainly to DTRv6 which has been my best model so far - all on experimental mode

**motorways/highways:**

not bad, seems to do a little boost now when you change lanes to overtake which is nice - but lane changes seem to sometimes just fail especially lane changes to the right. i've seen it do it completely fine, not do it at all or even go halfway inbetween both lanes and just sit there for a moment before moving back again.

speed control is decent, doesn't gradually slow down for no reason like gWMv3 and SP and actually hits the speed target, but it like to brake really late when approaching a lead vehicle, not quite enough to set off my cars early collision warning but probably not far off, i'd certainly be a bit scared if i saw my car behind going that fast towards me

steering i've had no problem with (other than the lane changes) but that's been good on motorways in basically every model

**90+ degree turns (note: turn desires is on):**

note that i've generally been using manual speed control for this (e.g. 0mph on TACC and using pedal to go), but i have managed to also get it to do some completely on its own too

very inconsistent in my testing, seems to somewhat depend on the width of the road its turning from/into, thinner roads it massively oversteers but very wide roads it can understeer

sometimes it can also do both, understeer and then overcorrect ending up in the oncoming lane which isn't great

hard to judge against DTRv6 here, i think maybe better in some scenarios, worse in others

**country lanes:**

had very good experience with this, probably on par with if not exceeding DTRv6, takes turns nicely and can slow down for tighter turns, not always but more consistently than before i feel

seems to be more cautious than DTRv6 about accelerating to the set speed limit (e.g. 60mph), but will eventually get there if conditions are good

**local roads / parked car avoidance:**

local roads is another strong point of this model, it doesn't always want to go around parked cars, but it will usually stop instead for them unlike DTRv6 which sometimes wanted to go into them

**stop and go traffic:**

very good on this model, accelerates with a decent boost from a stop when a lead vehicle moves and gradually comes to a stop behind them in stop and go traffic. does leave fairly large gaps though as it doesn't accelerate/stop very hard though which in multi-lane situations could get you cut-off sometimes potentially

**traffic lights:**

traffic lights are definitely not solved, but they are better vs DTRv6, if there are other vehicles already stopped in another lane i've found it usually does stop - and if it's approaching a red light at fairly low speed from a reasonable distance it can come to a full stop completely on its own

going on a green light works well with a lead vehicle, but on its own it struggles a lot still, but i have found this to be slightly better than DTRv6 which will basically never move from standstill without a kick 

**roundabouts / turning circles:**

it does pretty well at roundabouts in my testing, but it can struggle on very small roundabouts (e.g. ones that are just painted on), physical roundabouts with a barrier tend to work reasonably well as long as you are indicating correctly and have turn desires on too. very big roundabouts also works decently, but they're essentially just multi-lane very curved roads anyway. it does have a tendency to understeer on larger roundabouts and put you in the outside lane even if you're turning to the right which can confuse other drivers

**overall:**

i think this model is a pretty decent one, especially if it's been trained exclusively off firehose data (or even just supplemented by it). i would say it's more capable but less reliable compared to DTRv6

messages.content:
I tried the Firehose model in Experimental Mode (E2E Long).
Compared to TCPv3, the longitudinal control feels more aggressive, but I haven’t experienced the strange, unexplained slowdowns that sometimes happen with TCPv3. As a result, I’ve been enjoying much smoother cruising overall.
That said, TCPv3 is otherwise an extremely well-tuned and skillful driving model, so if those mysterious slowdowns were resolved, I think it would easily become the best model.
For lateral control, TCPv3 still feels smoother to me.
These impressions are with NNLC enabled on both.
After all this time Firehose is still my favorite lat-only model on both my Toyota and Hyundai.

https://commaai.github.io/model_reports/816ce390-c41a-42fa-a5df-f393cbe2dcc4/400/

You can check various reports on the Firehose models here, and once again, the behavior of E2E long really stands out.
For lateral control, the latest WMIv6 seems to perform very well, but when it comes to E2E long, I don’t know of any model that clearly outperforms Firehose.

After testing the models in the order WMIv6 → WMIv3 → WMIv2, and experiencing issues with acceleration and some steering instability, coming back to Firehose honestly feels like returning home — a sense of comfort and stability.

Aside from the acceleration issues, WMIv6 is an excellent model overall, and I really hope the comma team can overcome this remaining challenge.
